text: Recent visitor feedback indicates frustration with the timed ticketing system, especially from those who traveled long distances and were turned away without reservations or flexibility. Several reviews mention the high admission cost, particularly for families. There are also concerns about crowding and difficulty navigating the site, including poor signage for handicap parking and limited shuttle availability. Some visitors expressed disappointment with the focus on AI elements in the exhibits, feeling it detracted from learning about Theodore Roosevelt. Positive comments often highlight the building’s architecture and the interactive exhibits, but these do not fully offset the issues raised.

windows.7: Visitors over the past week have expressed frustration with the timed entry system, particularly the strict reservation requirement that led to some being turned away despite low attendance. Several reviewers compared this policy unfavorably to other presidential libraries that allow walk-in visits. There were also comments about staff interactions, with some visitors feeling the staff lacked flexibility or hospitality when handling reservation issues. A few mentions touched on the interactive exhibits and interpretive elements, but these were less prominent. Overall, the main concern centers on access and customer service related to the timed ticketing process.
